title: test-0116-SOC-CIV-GOVERNMENT
passage: A government is responsible for making decisions and implementing laws to manage a country. In a democracy, the government is elected by the people, but it must protect the rights of all citizens, not just the majority. This means that even if a group has many supporters, they cannot ignore the needs or rights of smaller groups. Governance happens at three levels: the local level, the state level, and the national level. The local government manages village or town affairs, but it operates under the rules and framework set by the national government, ensuring the whole country follows a unified system. Decisions made at the national level affect everyone, while state and local governments handle specific regional needs. In the past, monarchies were common, where a king or queen held all power. While some monarchs were indeed harsh, many were focused on the welfare of their subjects and worked to maintain order. Today, we use the system of universal adult franchise, which allows all citizens who are 18 years or older to vote. This is different from saying everyone in the country votes, as children and non-citizens are excluded. By voting, people choose representatives who make decisions on their behalf, ensuring that the government remains accountable to the public and functions within the law.
summary: A government makes decisions and follows laws to manage a country. The local government helps manage village or town affairs, but it follows the rules and framework set by the national government. At the national level, decisions affect everyone. At the local level, decisions are handled by the government.
